description: Positive detector cases: inputs that MUST redact. Each case's 'input' is materialized to a Python value (kind 'text' is a plain string scanned by redact_text; kind 'value' is a JSON value — possibly containing $$bytes_b64 / $$latin1 marker objects standing for byte strings — redacted by redact_value with the optional 'protected' paths). 'expected' is the exact redacted value, 'expected_counts' the exact per-category detector counts, and 'expected_affected_fields' the exact masked value-position count. The secret_key_spellings table lists every key spelling the secret-key detector must mask (both separator spellings the brief requires plus the concatenated spellings the design's optional-separator pattern also matches).

cases.name: pem-private-key-block
cases.input:
attached key:
-----BEGIN RSA PRIVATE KEY-----
MIIEpAIBAAKCAQEA0w3JkQrQxw==
-----END RSA PRIVATE KEY-----
use tls

cases.name: authorization-bearer-header
cases.note: The header name, separator, and scheme are preserved; only the credentials are masked.

cases.name: authorization-header-lowercase
cases.note: Header detection is case-insensitive and has no minimum credential length.

cases.name: standalone-bearer-value
cases.note: Standalone bearer values count under the auth_header category and keep the scheme.

cases.name: nested-secret-key
cases.note: Field names are preserved; only the assigned value is masked, at any depth.

cases.name: secret-key-with-structured-value
cases.note: The whole value assigned to a secret key is masked; it is never scanned as leaves.

cases.name: textual-password-assignment
cases.note: An unquoted textual value ends at whitespace; the key and separator are preserved.

cases.name: textual-json-style-quoted-assignment
cases.note: Malformed JSON text: quoted keys and quoted values keep their quotes; the key assignment masks the whole value before token detectors run.

cases.name: textual-colon-assignment-unquoted
cases.note: An unquoted value ends at semicolon as well as whitespace.

cases.name: textual-single-quoted-assignment
cases.note: A single-quoted value may contain spaces and keeps its quote style.

cases.name: textual-empty-quoted-assignment
cases.note: Any quoted value — empty included — is a value; masking has no non-empty guard.

cases.name: textual-uppercase-key-assignment
cases.note: Key-spelling matching is case-insensitive; the original key spelling is preserved.

cases.name: textual-suffix-key-assignment
cases.note: A spelling appearing as the tail of a larger unquoted key still masks its value; the unmatched key prefix survives outside the match.

cases.name: textual-quoted-compound-key-assignment
cases.note: Quoted keys tolerate a spelling suffix; surrounding quotes and delimiters are preserved.

cases.name: textual-mixed-header-and-assignment
cases.note: Two spans masked in one text value count two detections but one affected field.

cases.name: connection-string-password
cases.note: Scheme, user, and host are preserved; only the password is masked.

cases.name: connection-string-empty-user-password
cases.note: Empty-user userinfo (redis://:password@host) still carries a credential; the user part is optional.

cases.name: unterminated-pem-block
cases.note: A BEGIN marker without its matching END is a private-key fragment; it masks through the end of the text.

cases.name: openai-sk-token
cases.note: sk- requires at least 16 trailing characters.

cases.name: github-classic-token
cases.note: ghp_ requires at least 20 alphanumeric characters.

cases.name: github-fine-grained-token
cases.note: github_pat_ requires at least 20 alphanumeric/underscore characters.

cases.name: slack-bot-token
cases.note: xox[baprs]- requires at least 10 trailing characters.

cases.name: aws-access-key-id
cases.note: AKIA requires exactly 16 uppercase-alphanumeric characters.

cases.name: structured-token-in-note
cases.note: Non-secret string leaves are scanned textually.

cases.name: invalid-utf8-bytes-root
cases.note: Latin-1 described bytes that are not valid UTF-8 use the binary marker.

cases.name: secret-keyed-bytes
cases.note: The key detector fires; the marker reflects the byte-string value kind.

cases.name: multiple-token-spans
cases.note: Matches count per detection; affected fields count per changed value position.

cases.name: protected-dotted-path-partial
cases.note: A dotted path protects exactly that location; the same field name elsewhere is still masked.
